summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca), signed the ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1 and its IP, configured sshd via HostCertificate, and validated that a client trusting only the CA (@cert-authority line, no pinned host key) connects successfully with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, while a client with no CA trust and no pinned key is rejected. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id/service baseline, rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified CA-based cert trust still works post-restart. All temporary test keys/known_hosts artifacts were cleaned up; the CA and host certificate configuration remain in place.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/sshd version and existing host key files
Generated ED25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca (private) and ssh_ca.pub (public)
Signed /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate valid 10 years for principals node1 and 10.100.10.10
Added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd
Verified via ssh -vv that the server offers the signed certificate to clients
Positive test: connected using only a known_hosts @cert-authority trust line (no pinned host key), succeeded
Negative control: connected with empty known_hosts (no CA trust), confirmed strict host key checking rejects the connection
Cleaned up temporary test SSH keypair and authorized_keys/known_hosts entries
Captured pre-restart boot_id and sshd/cert health baseline
Rebooted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, sshd active, cert files and sshd_config directive intact
Re-ran full certificate-trust connection test post-restart to confirm persistence, then cleaned up test artifacts

evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca (CA private key) and ssh_ca.pub (CA public key)

evidence.requirement: Host key signed into a certificate by the CA
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub, producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/10.100.10.10, verified via ssh-keygen -L

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate
evidence.summary: Added HostCertificate directive, validated config with sshd -t, reloaded sshd, and confirmed via ssh -vv that the server actually offers the signed certificate on the wire

evidence.requirement: Client trusting the CA connects without pinning the host key
evidence.summary: known_hosts populated only with an @cert-authority line for the CA public key; ssh with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeded, proving trust via CA rather than a pinned key

evidence.requirement: Falsification: without CA trust, connection is rejected
evidence.summary: Same client against an empty known_hosts file failed with 'Host key verification failed', showing the earlier success came from CA trust
Captured boot_id 1f0657c2..., sshd active, and cert/CA files present before restart
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' command returned control before the connection dropped due to shutdown

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polled node1 (connection refused, then success) and confirmed boot_id changed to 5c821d10..., proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data (sshd, cert, CA config)
evidence.summary: sshd active, HostCertificate config line and cert/CA files intact post-restart, and end-to-end CA-based client connection succeeded again after reboot
